land.text: 'In 1543 it officially became the governorship of Michoacán'

successors.note: Spanish conquest: 'lost its independence to the Spanish in 1530'; Tangaxoan II was killed by Nuño de Guzmán in 1530. Cliopatria keeps the Michoacán row to 1533.

capitals.name: Pátzcuaro
capitals.note: 'Tariacuri ruled from Patzcuaro city' while his sons Hiripan and Tangaxuan held Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan (c. 1300). The end year is the death of Tariacuri 'around 1350'; the page does not date the move of the court. Coordinates are the town's (not from a page).

capitals.name: Tzintzuntzan (Ts'intsúntsani)
capitals.note: 'The Purepecha capital was located at Tzintzuntzan', on the banks of Lake Patzcuaro; the page dates neither the move nor the dynasty's seat (reading: after Tariacuri). The coordinates are the gazetteer's historic site.

correction.text: Tariacuri's dominion in the Patzcuaro basin: 'installed his sons Hiripan and Tangaxuan as lords of Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan'; 'By the death of Tariacuri (around 1350), his lineage was in control of all the major centers around Lake Patzcuaro'

keyframe_review.note: 1305-1428, 5,634 km2 in Cliopatria. The shape (101.40-100.42 W, 18.22-18.99 N, 10 Guerrero and 10 Michoacan cells) lies in the Balsas lowlands and contains neither Tzintzuntzan nor Patzcuaro (the gazetteer finds no overlap with a 35 km disc round Tzintzuntzan); the Balsas was incorporated later ('first the sierra and then the Balsas River', undated). Corrected to the lake basin. The Cuitzeo expansion under Hiripan is undated and the Michoacan page puts the conquest of neighbours between 1401 and 1450, so it is left to the 1429 and 1440 shapes. No infobox area.

correction.text: The Cliopatria shape (Lake Cuitzeo side and the Balsas lowlands) together with the Patzcuaro basin: 'Hiripan continued the expansion into the area surrounding Lake Cuitzeo'; 'Conquest of neighboring tribes and territories occurred between 1401 and 1450'

keyframe_review.note: 1429-1439, 17,531 km2. Cliopatria's shape holds a Morelia cell (Lake Cuitzeo) but not the Patzcuaro basin, the heartland, so it is added. The Cuitzeo expansion is undated on the page.

1440-1449, 45,786 km2: 153 cells, now containing Tzintzuntzan and the whole lake basin (14 of 14 cells), 131 of Michoacan's 198 cells and 8 in Jalisco. 'Conquest of neighboring tribes and territories occurred between 1401 and 1450' (Michoacan page); no year is given for any of them, so the 1440 jump is accepted as the sources' 1401-1450 spread. The Tarascan page's footnote gives '75,000 square kilometers' for A.D. 1450 against Cliopatria's 49,787 km2 for 1450 (ratio 0.66): within the factor.

1450-1458, 49,787 km2 (twelve Guerrero cells added, toward the Pacific). The footnote 'an empire that spanned 75,000 square kilometers of west Mexico' for A.D. 1450 is 1.5 times Cliopatria's area; the 75,000 figure matches the shapes from 1468 (74,593 km2).

1459-1462, 53,040 km2: 'In 1460 the Irechikwa reached the Pacific coast at Zacatula, advanced into the Toluca Valley' and northern Guanajuato. Cliopatria's shape has the coast but not the Toluca Valley (held by the Aztecs, contested 1455-1472) and only a Guanajuato cell.
1463-1467, 53,763 km2: three more Guerrero cells along the coast; the page gives no further year (page silent).

correction.text: Without Jalisco and Colima, which the Tarascan page has occupied later: 'Between 1480 and 1510, the Irechikwa occupied parts of present day Colima and Jalisco'

keyframe_review.note: 1468-1474, 74,593 km2 (+72 cells: 48 in Jalisco, 8 in Guanajuato, one in Colima). The page puts the Jalisco and Colima occupation in 1480-1510, not 1468; the shape's 75,000 km2 matches the footnote only if those are counted. Corrected to the shape without them until the occupation (ledger 1480). The Guanajuato cells are in the south of the state; the page's Guanajuato is the north (1460).

correction.text: Without Jalisco and Colima, as for 1468 (occupied 1480-1510 on the Tarascan page); the frontier towns taken by Axayacatl 'in the 1470s' pass to the Aztec shape

keyframe_review.note: 1475-1481, 73,429 km2: five cells lost on the eastern frontier, matching 'In the 1470s, Aztecs under Axayacatl captured a series of frontier towns'. Jalisco and Colima as for 1468.

1482-1496, 73,871 km2: Jalisco and Colima are in this shape; the page's occupation runs 1480-1510, so it is accepted as a snapshot of the process. 'From 1480 the Aztec ruler Ahuitzotl intensified the conflict'; King Zuangua 'repelled the attacks'.

1497-1520, 73,732 km2: the area at the Aztec frontier's last decades; 'At the time of the Spanish conquest, it was the second-largest state in Mesoamerica.' The occupation of Colima and Jalisco ends in 1510 (page). No page reports a change in 1497.

1521-1528, 73,902 km2: the kingdom still stands after the fall of Tenochtitlan. 'In 1522 a Spanish force under the leadership of Cristobal de Olid was sent into Purepecha territory'; the page does not say whether it held ground, and the status of the court between 1522 and 1529 is not on the pages read.

correction.text: The same shape, ending on 14 February 1530: 'the king was executed on February 14, 1530'; 'lost its independence to the Spanish in 1530'. The years 1531-1533 belong to the Spanish Empire

keyframe_review.note: 1529-1533 in Cliopatria; the page ends the kingdom in 1530. Shape unchanged, years cut: Tangaxoan II 'killed ... in 1530' by Nuño de Guzman (Michoacan page).

region.text: the Patzcuaro basin: Patzcuaro, Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan

ledger.note: c. 1300: Tariacuri founds the Tarascan state round Lake Patzcuaro. 'installed his sons Hiripan and Tangaxuan as lords of Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan respectively'; Tariacuri ruled from Patzcuaro; 'The kingdom was founded in the early 14th century' (infobox 'established 1300-1350'). The Michoacan page: he united the basin's polities 'over the course of c. 1300 to c. 1350'. 1305 is Cliopatria's year.

region.text: 'all the major centers around Lake Patzcuaro'

ledger.note: c. 1350: the whole Patzcuaro basin is one state. 'By the death of Tariacuri (around 1350), his lineage was in control of all the major centers around Lake Patzcuaro.'

Hiripan's Cuitzeo conquests. 'His son Hiripan continued the expansion into the area surrounding Lake Cuitzeo' (Tarascan page, no year); the Michoacan page puts the conquest of neighbours 'between 1401 and 1450'. Cliopatria's first shape with a Cuitzeo cell begins in 1429, which is the year used (page silent, confidence 1).

region.text: the neighbouring tribes and territories conquered between 1401 and 1450

ledger.note: Tarascan conquests grow the kingdom threefold. 'Conquest of neighboring tribes and territories occurred between 1401 and 1450' (Michoacan page, no year); the 1440 year is Cliopatria's jump (page silent, confidence 1). Hiripan and Tangaxuan I 'began to institutionalize the tributary system'.

1455: the Tarascans invade the Toluca Valley. 'In 1455, the Purepecha under their king Tzitzipandaquare had invaded the Toluca Valley, claiming lands previously conquered by Motecuzoma and Itzcoatl.' The Tarascan page dates the advance into the Toluca Valley to 1460. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: Toluca disc cut from 60 to 50 km: at 60 km it reached the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan)]

region.text: 'In 1460 the Irechikwa reached the Pacific coast at Zacatula'

ledger.note: 1460: the Tarascans reach the Pacific at Zacatula. 'In 1460 the Irechikwa reached the Pacific coast at Zacatula, advanced into the Toluca Valley.' Cliopatria adds the coastal Guerrero cells in 1450, 1459 and 1463.

1472: the Aztecs recover the Toluca Valley. 'In 1472, Axayacatl re-conquered the region and successfully defended it from Purepecha's attempts to take it back.' The Axayacatl page has 1474. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: Toluca disc cut from 60 to 50 km: at 60 km it reached the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan)]

region.text: frontier towns: 'In the 1470s, Aztecs under Axayacatl captured a series of frontier towns'

ledger.note: 1475: Aztec raiders take frontier towns of eastern Michoacan. 'In the 1470s, Aztecs under Axayacatl captured a series of frontier towns' (no year; 1475 is the year of Cliopatria's change, page silent, confidence 1).

1476: the Tarascans defeat Axayacatl. Axayacatl was 'finally defeated by the Tarascans of Michoacan in 1476' (Axayacatl page); the Aztec page records a second Tarascan victory in 1479 over 32,000 Aztec soldiers.

region.text: 'parts of present day Colima and Jalisco'

ledger.note: 1480: the Tarascans begin to occupy Colima and Jalisco. 'Between 1480 and 1510, the Irechikwa occupied parts of present day Colima and Jalisco.' The page gives the span, not the stages; the process starts with the page's 1480 and ends in 1510. Cliopatria shows the whole of it from 1468. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region was the whole of Jalisco and Colima (about 72,000 km2 of cells); the page says 'parts of present day Colima and Jalisco', so it is now their intersection with Cliopatria's 1482 shape (49 cells, about 12,400 km2)]
1515: the last Aztec invasion fails. 'In 1515, Aztec armies commanded by the Tlaxcalan general Tlahuicole invaded the Purepecha Empire once again' and 'failed to take any territory'.

1522: a Spanish force under Cristobal de Olid enters Purepecha territory. 'In 1522 a Spanish force under the leadership of Cristobal de Olid was sent into Purepecha territory.' The page does not say it held ground; the Michoacan page says 'The first Spaniard to the area was Cristobal de Olid'. Contest as the start of the conquest, confidence 2.
February 1530: the kingdom falls. 'the king was executed on February 14, 1530'; 'lost its independence to the Spanish in 1530'.

14 February 1530: Nuño de Guzman kills Tangaxoan II and the Tarascan kingdom passes to New Spain. 'killed Tanganxoan II in 1530' (Michoacan page); 'In 1543 it officially became the governorship of Michoacan' (Tarascan page).
14 February 1530: end of the Tarascan state, 'the last king of a sovereign kingdom, Tangaxuan II'. The page's infobox gives 'conquered by New Spain 1520-1530'; Cliopatria keeps the row to 1533.

wars.name: Tarascan conquests of the neighbours
belligerents: Neighbouring tribes and territories (Cuitzeo, Zacapu, Balsas, Zacatula, Colima, Jalisco)
wars.outcome: 'Conquest of neighboring tribes and territories occurred between 1401 and 1450'; Zacatula on the Pacific in 1460; Colima and Jalisco partly occupied in 1480-1510.
wars.note: Under Hiripan, Tangaxuan I and Tzitzipandaquare; the pages date none of the first campaigns.

wars.name: Aztec-Tarascan wars
wars.outcome: The Tarascans invaded the Toluca Valley in 1455 and lost it in 1472; they defeated Axayacatl in 1476 and 1479 and an Aztec invasion in 1515 'failed to take any territory'.
wars.note: The Tarascan page: 'From 1480 the Aztec ruler Ahuitzotl intensified the conflict'; King Zuangua repelled the attacks; the Aztecs fortified their frontier with military centres such as Cutzamala.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Michoacán
wars.outcome: A Spanish force under Cristobal de Olid entered in 1522; Nuño de Guzman killed Tangaxoan II in 1530 ('the king was executed on February 14, 1530'); the land became the governorship of Michoacán in 1543.
wars.note: The pages say nothing on the terms between 1522 and 1529 (whether Tangaxoan II paid tribute to Cortes).

certainty.note: A tributary kingdom with fortified frontier posts; no border is dated or surveyed. The Aztec-Tarascan frontier is the one stable line from the 1470s and is still approximate.

sources.title: Tarascan state
sources.note: Identity, c. 1300 founding, 1350, capital Tzintzuntzan, expansions of 1460 and 1480-1510, Aztec wars, 75,000 km2 for A.D. 1450, Spanish conquest 1522-1530.

sources.title: Michoacán
sources.note: Cliopatria's article for the row: c. 1300-c. 1350 under Tariacuri, conquests 1401-1450, Nuño de Guzman 1530, province.

sources.title: Aztec Empire
sources.note: Purepecha invasion of the Toluca Valley 1455, Axayacatl 1472, defeat of 1479, Tlahuicole 1515.

sources.title: Axayacatl
sources.note: Defeat by the Tarascans of Michoacan in 1476; Toluca Valley 1474.

notes: Four pages (budget five). (1) CLIOPATRIA SHAPE 1305-1439 IS MISPLACED: the 1305 shape (5,634 km2) and the 1429 shape (17,531 km2) lie east and south of Lake Patzcuaro and contain no Patzcuaro-basin cell, the kingdom's heartland; the dossier replaces the first and adds the basin to the second. The shapes from 1440 contain the basin. (2) JALISCO AND COLIMA: Cliopatria has 48 Jalisco cells from 1468, the Tarascan page has 'Between 1480 and 1510' for the occupation; the 1468 and 1475 shapes are cut, the later ones accepted. (3) END 14 February 1530, not 1533; Cliopatria's Spanish Empire row touches the Michoacan shape from 1521 to 1533. The terms between Olid's 1522 expedition and 1530 are not on the pages read. (4) AREA: the Tarascan page's footnote '75,000 square kilometers' for A.D. 1450 matches Cliopatria's shapes from 1468 (74,593 km2), not the 1450 shape (49,787 km2). (5) No ruler list with dates is on the pages (Tariacuri, Hiripan, Tangaxuan I, Tzitzipandaquare, Zuangua, Tangaxuan II are named without reign years), so identity.rulers is omitted. (6) Capital dates: Patzcuaro until about 1350 and Tzintzuntzan after are my reading of 'Tariacuri ruled from Patzcuaro' and 'The Purepecha capital was located at Tzintzuntzan'. (7) The Michoacan page is Cliopatria's Wikipedia field (the modern state's article); the state's own article is 'Tarascan state' (the wikipedia field is kept as Cliopatria gives it). (8) The Tangaxoan II page would not load under the three spellings tried (Tangaxoan_II, Tangáxoan_II, Tang%C3%A1xoan_II). (9) Aztec-side counterparts are the slug aztec-triple-alliance.
